Guide

Is IPTV legal in the UK?

Short answer: IPTV as a technology is completely legal. Whether a particular service is legal depends on whether it has permission to show what it streams.

See plans from £7Ask for a free trial

The technology is legal

IPTV simply means TV delivered over the internet. BBC iPlayer, ITVX, BT TV, Virgin Media Stream and Sky Glass all use it. Owning a Smart TV, a Firestick or an Android box is legal, and so is using player apps such as IPTV Smarters Pro or TiviMate.

What makes a service illegal

The question is not the technology but the rights. Channels, films and sport are protected by copyright, and broadcasters pay for the right to show them. A service that streams that content without permission from the rights holders is infringing copyright, however professional its website looks.

What UK law says

  • The Copyright, Designs and Patents Act 1988 makes it a criminal offence to distribute copyrighted material without permission. Since the Digital Economy Act 2017, the maximum sentence for online infringement is 10 years.
  • Sellers of unlicensed streams and “fully loaded” boxes have also been prosecuted for fraud and conspiracy, and some have been jailed.
  • For viewers, knowingly watching unlicensed pay-TV streams can also break the law. Rights holders and the Federation Against Copyright Theft (FACT) have contacted and warned individual viewers of illegal services.

You still need a TV licence

In the UK you need a TV licence to watch or record live TV on any channel, on any device, including through an IPTV app, and to use BBC iPlayer. That is separate from whatever you pay an IPTV provider.

How to check a service

  • Does it name who runs it, with a postal address and contact details?
  • Does it have written terms and a refund policy?
  • Can you pay by a normal method, or only by gift card or crypto?
  • Is the price realistic for what it claims to include?
  • Will it answer your questions about what is included before you pay?

If the answer to several of these is no, walk away.

FAQ

Questions people ask

Is IPTV legal in the UK?

Yes, the technology is legal. A service is only legal if it has permission from the rights holders for what it streams.

Is a Firestick legal?

Yes. The device and mainstream apps are legal. What matters is where the streams you load into it come from.

Can I get in trouble for watching IPTV in the UK?

Watching licensed services is fine. Knowingly watching unlicensed pay-TV streams can break the law, and some viewers of illegal services have received warnings.

Do I need a TV licence for IPTV?

Yes, if you watch or record live TV as it is broadcast, or use BBC iPlayer.
